A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Vision-RWKV work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The complete v1 PDF ends after its references despite mentioning an appendix; v3 includes Appendix A.1–A.3. This is a document-content difference, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, detection, segmentation, ablation, efficiency, and MAE pretraining results in Section 4, Tables 2–5, and Figures 1 and 3.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds resolution-robustness and Vision Mamba comparisons in Appendices A.2–A.3.

M1.justification: The architecture, Bi-WKV and Q-Shift equations, model configurations, and stabilization components remain unchanged. Removing vertical shifts for MAE clarifies the previously described bidirectional adaptation. The added backward-pass and numerical-stability details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: ImageNet-1K/22K, Bamboo-47K, COCO, ADE20K, and the existing tasks are retained. Appendix A.2 adds an accuracy test under train–test resolution mismatch: training at 224×224 and evaluating through 1024×1024. v1's resolution sweeps measured efficiency rather than classification robustness.

E2.justification: v3 adds Vim-T/S/B classification comparisons in Table 7 and Vision Mamba kernel timing in Figure 5; Vim-L is marked unavailable. The existing benchmark comparators remain. PyTorch attention and FlashAttention already appeared in v1's Figure 3.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes large-model ImageNet-22K pretraining from 30 to 90 epochs, substantially increasing the reported training budget. Appendices A.2–A.3 introduce fixed-training-resolution robustness evaluation and an A100 kernel-timing sweep over 224–1024 resolution. The principal downstream protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a resolution-sensitivity analysis across tiny, small, and base models, testing whether accuracy survives higher-resolution inference without corresponding training. Existing token-shift and bidirectionality ablations, effective-receptive-field analysis, and MAE analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its results. The added appendix comparisons continue the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: VRWKV-L accuracy changes from 85.3% to 86.0%, and its MAE result from 85.5% to 86.2%, alongside longer pretraining. New results include resolution-robustness curves and Vim comparisons. Figure 3 extends PyTorch timing results and labels 230×/120× speedups against PyTorch; v1's 2.8×/2.7× labels concern FlashAttention. Tables 3–5 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: v1 asserts linear-complexity backpropagation and refers to an absent appendix. v3 supplies state recurrences and initializations, gradient equations, and a backward-complexity argument in Appendix A.1, Table 6, and Equations 10–14. This substantially expands the mathematical documentation, although Table 6 does not consistently preserve Equation 6's decay normalization.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens classification performance from matching ViT to surpassing it, while explicitly qualifying speed and memory advantages as applying to high-resolution inputs. The introduction updates the large-model accuracy claim. The central contribution remains a scalable, linear-complexity visual alternative to ViT.

C2.justification: v3 newly discusses inefficient PyTorch Q-Shift implementation and Bi-WKV's lack of FlashAttention-style hardware optimization. It interprets the appendix results as evidence of resolution robustness and attributes scalability relative to Vim to stability design. These extend the existing explanations and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies previously missing implementation-relevant state updates, initialization, and safe-exponential calculations. v3 clarifies the MAE shift adaptation and expands its availability statement from code to code and models. Conversely, it drops v1's explicit channel/head configuration description for the attention-timing comparison.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Mini-InternVL, hierarchically gated recurrent networks, and online softmax normalization, while removing the BERT/PALs citation. Positioning against Vim and VMamba becomes more specific about scale and training stability. The broader related-work framework is retained.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. Local rewrites refine the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and classification/efficiency discussions. v3 also adds appendix organization and acknowledgments, updates author information, and switches to author–year citations.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a substantially different ICLR layout, resizing and repositioning displays throughout. It redraws Figure 3, adds Figures 4–5 and Tables 6–7, places the MAE result in Table 2, and introduces Window columns in Tables 3–4. Figures 1–2 and the receptive-field images are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens validation with resolution-robustness tests and direct Vision Mamba comparisons, while supplying previously omitted backward-pass and numerical-stability details. These gains are tempered by inconsistent decay normalization in Table 6 and reduced timing-configuration disclosure. The higher classification accuracy also accompanies tripled pretraining, rather than establishing a same-setting advance.
